structured_output.what_is_happening: A 13-minute-old copycat "e/acc" token. It launched on a Meteora virtual curve and migrated immediately, and it now trades on PumpSwap. It rode a burst of roughly 1,000 unique buyers in about 15 minutes, apparently tied to a beffjezos X post ("from crime szn to merci szn"). The canonical e/acc token is already worth $17.7M. At detection this one had dropped 43% in 5 minutes. GeckoTerminal's latest 5-minute window shows activity collapsing: only $2.8k volume and 64 buys, against $61k and 1,375 buys over 15 minutes.

narrative.description: This is a derivative play on the Beff Jezos / e/acc story, using a specific tweet as its link. The main e/acc narrative is already captured by a $17.7M canonical token. That token's page is even listed as this coin's 'website'.
narrative.why_spreading: Traders quickly jumped on a fresh Beff Jezos tweet and launched several same-name coins within seconds of each other. The spike looks like sniping of the tweet, not a growing community.

token_connection.why_this_token: The only link is the tweet URL used as its X handle. The name is identical to the established canonical e/acc token.
token_connection.competing_tokens: Canonical e/acc CbcyNo… ($17.7M mcap, $600k liquidity). Two other E/ACC clones, one launched 13 seconds after this one (EVVL…).

authenticity.evidence: About 1,000 unique buyers is broad, and GMGN shows few bundlers or snipers and a 0% bot rate. On the other hand, the image is duplicated 26 times, the dev has closed out (creator_close), the ticker is shared by several clones, and the buying burst was highly concentrated in time. That pattern is typical of tweet-sniping bots and copy traders.
authenticity.uncertainty: No X data, so I can't tell whether Beff Jezos or anyone notable engaged with this particular contract.

structural_risks: RugCheck flags 100% of the LP as unlocked; GMGN reports the LP as burned (conflicting data)
One unlabelled address holds 80% of supply, probably a pool or curve account, but not confirmed
Dev has closed out; one earlier launch peaked at about $212k
Same-name clones split the attention, and a dominant canonical token exists
Momentum collapsed right after the first spike

A $70k mcap with $24k liquidity and more than 1,000 holders is a real base, and small tweet-driven coins sometimes put in a second leg once the first dump is absorbed.

structured_output.thesis: This is a tweet-snipe clone of an established $17.7M e/acc token. The buying burst has already peaked and it is dumping, the latest 5-minute volume is tiny, and the dev has exited. It is unlikely to double from entry, and there is a meaningful chance it bleeds out or dies.
